name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Fixes two live causes of federated playback dying with 'Playback Error' even though the content was playable. (1) When the primary source's server refused to mint a playback token (content unshared or deleted on the friend since the last sync, or the friend temporarily down), the stream hard-failed - even when the exact same movie/show sat on a second federated server via dedup. That redundancy was the whole point of dedup, but nothing ever fell back to it. The proxy stream path now tries the same cache entry's other sources, with per-remote-user access rules re-checked against each candidate server, both on the initial build and on the 401/403 re-mint path. Verified against the exact live failure: a token-mint 403 from one friend now transparently serves from the sibling source instead of killing ffmpeg with exit code 8. (2) 'No cached Plex item id ... a library refresh is needed' could permanently break a Plex item whose stamped URL no longer matched the cache index after a dedup re-key left the (server, item) pair unindexed - the native id was intact in the entry, only the lookup path was stale. The lookup now self-heals by scanning for the entry by remote item id and re-indexing it, so the next play is O(1) again. 301 tests, all green.
